item.title: Bad Bunny Moves to Overturn Ruling in Reggaeton Case: ‘They Have Assembled a Frankenstein’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to "Trending on Billboard", the podcast that brings you the latest news and updates from the music industry. I'm your host, [Name], and today we're talking about a lawsuit that's been making waves in the reggaeton world.
[Music transitions to a brief reggaeton clip]
Host: Bad Bunny is fighting back against a lawsuit that claims he and dozens of other artists infringed on the copyright of the dembow rhythm, a fundamental beat in reggaeton music. The lawsuit, filed by reggae duo Steely & Clevie, alleges that their 1989 song "Fish Market" is the origin of the dembow rhythm.
[Music transitions back to the host]
Host: But Bad Bunny's lawyers are arguing that the case has a major flaw. They claim that the alleged proprietary beat doesn't exist entirely in any of the three songs that allegedly spawned it, including "Fish Market", "Dem Bow", and "Pounder (Dub Mix II)". In fact, they're calling it a "Frankenstein" copyright, implying that it's been cobbled together from different sources.
[Music transitions to a brief clip of Bad Bunny's music]
Host: The judge had previously ruled that only a jury could decide whether the dembow rhythm is copyrightable, which could lead to years of litigation. But Bad Bunny's team is asking the judge to reconsider, or alternatively, allow them to appeal the ruling to a federal appeals court.
[Music transitions back to the host]
Host: Steely & Clevie's attorney has responded, saying that Bad Bunny's team is pushing a "false narrative" and that they hope the court will quickly deny the motion.
[Music transitions to a brief reggaeton clip]
Host: The outcome of this case could have major implications for the reggaeton industry, with over 2,000 songs potentially affected. We'll be keeping an eye on this story and bringing you updates as it develops.
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to "Trending on Billboard". Join us next time for more news and updates from the music industry.
